source_name: Unioni Financiar Prishtinë sh.p.k. (UFP) — Western Union principal agent for Kosovo
why_relevant: Largest remittance actor in the cell: WU agent since 2000 with a stated 170+ location network. Its sub-agent recruitment page, tariff page and location list expose network size, expansion and the counter technology it deploys — a direct buyer of agent terminals, till software and KYC tooling. Tenders will be private, so the corporate site and its news are the visible surface.

source_name: Moneta sh.p.k. — MoneyGram agent / non-bank financial institution, Kosovo
why_relevant: Second major remittance NBFI in the cell (MoneyGram network plus bill payments). A contract party for agent-network software, cash-handling and compliance tooling; its branch/agent list is the observable footprint.

source_name: OneFor (OneFor Holding GmbH, Düsseldorf) — Kosovo-licensed non-bank financial institution / digital payments app
why_relevant: Diaspora-focused wallet licensed by BQK as an IFJB — a new-generation buyer of card issuing, wallet, KYC and remittance-rail technology. Launch coverage in Albanian media is the practical way to date its licence and partner stack, since it publishes no tenders.

source_name: Swinto — fintech payments platform launched in Kosovo and Switzerland
why_relevant: Prishtina-founded transfer/payments platform in the diaspora corridor; a contract party for card, wallet and compliance vendors. Telegrafi/Express launch pieces are the main dated public record of such firms.

source_name: IBAS — e-money institution serving Kosovo (SEPA transfers, remittances, Mastercard)
why_relevant: Self-described licensed e-money institution offering Kosovo remittances and Mastercard issuing — i.e. a buyer of BIN sponsorship, card processing and issuing-platform services. Its product pages reveal the scheme and processor relationships.

source_name: Paysera Kosova — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Local franchise of a large Lithuanian EMI operating in Kosovo; LinkedIn is where such firms announce local launches, partner integrations, POS/QR acceptance products and hiring for payments infrastructure roles — a leading indicator of what they are building or buying.

source_name: Telekomi i Kosovës Sh.A. (Vala) — corporate notices / njoftime
why_relevant: State-owned mobile operator whose payment-adjacent arms (top-up, billing, OCS platform, mobile money potential) are procured under the public procurement law; its own notices page carries clarifications and responses to procurement controversies that name winning vendors and procedure types.

source_name: Syri.net — investigative economy desk on Telekomi i Kosovës procurement
why_relevant: Kosovo media routinely surface negotiated-without-publication contracts that never appear as open tenders — exactly the procurement mode used for payment/billing platform extensions. Concrete example: an OCS billing-platform contract to Intracom (Skopje) worth ~EUR 146,900.

source_name: Projektligji / Ligji për shërbimet e pagesave (Law No. 08/L-328 and the 2026 draft) — Office of the Prime Minister
why_relevant: The payment services law is what creates the PI/EMI/AISP categories and the BQK public register; draft amendments circulated by the government signal the next wave of licensing and of open-banking/instant-payment obligations that drive vendor selection.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës — The Kosovo Banker (issuu archive)
why_relevant: Industry magazine where acquirers, processors and fintechs describe deployments (contactless, tapXphone/softPOS, open APIs) and where vendors advertise — an efficient, dated record of who supplies whom in Kosovo payments, including non-bank players partnering with banks.

source_name: World Bank corporate procurement — 'Electronic Payment Acceptance in Kosovo' (RFX 2018683) and related IFI tender streams
why_relevant: Donor and IFI programmes are a real contracting channel for Kosovo payments modernisation (acceptance networks, digitising government payments) and, unlike private PI procurement, they publish notices and awards openly.

source_name: BIS Review — speeches of the BQK Governor on banks, fintechs and payments digitalisation
why_relevant: Governor speeches state supervisory priorities and forthcoming payment-infrastructure projects (instant payments, fintech licensing, acceptance expansion) months before procurement appears — an early-warning layer for this cell.

source_name: Posta e Kosovës / NPOSTA — postal payment and counter services terms
why_relevant: The postal operator runs a nationwide counter network used for bill payment and cash services — a publicly-owned, procurement-law-bound buyer of counter terminals, cash handling and payment integration, and a possible agent for remittance firms.

source_name: PaymentProviders.io — Kosovo country directory of payment providers
why_relevant: Commercial directory listing providers claiming Kosovo coverage; useful only as a name-generation seed for the actor map, since inclusion is not evidence of a BQK licence.

source_name: Quipu GmbH — News / press (ProCredit group IT arm)
why_relevant: Quipu is the in-house/affiliated IT vendor of the ProCredit group and publicly announced delivering ProCredit Bank Kosovo's new mobile banking app and core-banking integration overhaul. Confirmed Kosovo-specific supply-side announcement found here — exactly the 'winner announces what the buyer never discloses' pattern.

source_name: Payten — News & Events (ASEE payments arm: POS, ATM, e-commerce, processing)
why_relevant: Payten (Asseco SEE group) is one of the dominant POS/ATM/processing suppliers across the Western Balkans and routinely publishes bank-by-bank win announcements (e.g. ATM delivery contracts, SoftPOS launches in neighbouring markets). Fetched listing confirmed live and structured; Kosovo items should surface here when they occur.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — News & Events
why_relevant: ASEE is the largest SEE banking-software vendor (core banking, digital channels, ATM/POS via Payten) and has a registered Kosovo entity (ASSECO SEE SH.P.K., Prishtina). Its news stream carries bank-contract announcements by name across the region; Kosovo wins would be announced here or in the Kosovo entity's channels.

source_name: Asseco SEE Kosovo (ASSECO SEE SH.P.K.) — STIKK member profile
why_relevant: Confirms a local Kosovo legal entity for the region's biggest banking-software vendor, giving a local company name to hunt in procurement registers, court/business registry filings and local press. Member profiles typically carry the local site, contacts and self-described client sectors.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association member directory
why_relevant: Highest-value pointer for this cell: ~100+ Kosovo ICT companies, including the local integrators and resellers who actually sign bank contracts (Asseco SEE Kosovo, Cacttus, LinkPlus IT, Panamic ICT and others). Snowballing the directory yields the vendor set whose own sites/press must then be monitored for Kosovo bank wins.

source_name: ICT Kosovo company directory (ictkosovo.eu)
why_relevant: Second, independent Kosovo ICT company registry (donor/cluster-run). Useful to cross-check STIKK and catch vendors not in STIKK; entries carry company profiles and reference claims that can reveal bank clients.

source_name: KIESA — Kosovo Exporters Directory (Ministry of Industry/Investment agency)
why_relevant: State-run exporters directory lists Kosovo ICT firms with self-declared capabilities and references; combined with STIKK it completes the local vendor/integrator actor map for supply-side monitoring.

source_name: Cacttus (Kosovo system integrator) — corporate site / references
why_relevant: Self-described leading Kosovar ICT integrator (est. 2003) covering Kosovo, Albania and the region across system integration, security and business solutions — a plausible prime or sub on bank infrastructure contracts. Its own references/news pages are where such wins would be publicised.

source_name: InfoSoft Systems Kosovo (InfoSoft Group Albania) — company / projects pages
why_relevant: InfoSoft Systems Prishtina (est. 2014, part of InfoSoft Group Albania) states it works with the banking and telecom sector and has completed 50+ projects in system integration, cybersecurity and automation — a regional integrator whose Kosovo bank work is announced on its own site rather than by the buyer.
